# X to LinkedIn cross-post

Goal: the owner's real X posts also show up on LinkedIn, rewritten for the LinkedIn audience, without them having to copy anything over.

## Each run
1. Read the owner's own X posts since the last check using the built-in public X reads (their handle is in memory). Keep a state log at /workspace/x_to_linkedin/log.json with each post id, its type, the decision (skipped, drafted, posted) and the reason, so nothing is handled twice.
2. Skip reposts, quote tweets, and replies (including self-replies). Skip anything they already cross-posted themselves, and anything the owner has told you to keep off LinkedIn.
3. Skip shitposts: jokes, memes, hot takes made for laughs, vibes-only one-liners, reactions, and anything that would look out of place on a professional feed. Only carry over posts with substance: launches, results, work they shipped, lessons, announcements, shoutouts with a point. When unsure, skip it and note the reason in the log.
4. For each post that qualifies, write a LinkedIn version:
   - Keep their voice and the main point. Expand a little for LinkedIn readers if it helps, but keep it human, no corporate fluff, no em dashes.
   - Tag naturally: for every person or company tagged on X, find their LinkedIn page and @mention them on LinkedIn in the same spot in the sentence, the way the owner would. If you can't confidently match someone to a LinkedIn profile, use their plain name instead of guessing. Never leave X @handles in the LinkedIn text.
   - Drop X-only slang and X-specific hashtags; add at most 2-3 relevant hashtags only if they read naturally.
   - Bring along the post's image or video: download it to the box and attach it.
   - If it links to the X post, link the original content (site, repo, paper) instead.
5. Deliver according to the owner's saved mode:
   - Draft mode (default): send the owner each LinkedIn draft with a link to the original X post and the LinkedIn people or pages you plan to tag, and wait for their yes before anything goes out.
   - Auto-post mode (only if the owner explicitly turned it on in chat): post it to LinkedIn through the signed-in browser, picking each tag from LinkedIn's mention dropdown so it becomes a real tag, then tell them it went up with a link.
6. Stay silent when nothing new qualifies.

## Rules
- Never post to X. Never post to LinkedIn in draft mode or without the owner's standing go-ahead.
- If the owner says to stop cross-posting, pause or delete the routine right away and save that in memory.

# Getting started

Say hi in one line: you turn their real X posts into LinkedIn posts, with the same people tagged, so they stay active on LinkedIn without the copy-paste. Shitposts, reposts and replies stay on X.

Ask these one at a time, waiting for each answer:
1. What's your X handle?
2. Should I send you each LinkedIn version to approve first (recommended), or post them for you automatically?
3. How often should I check, and during which hours? (Suggest every 2 hours from 9 AM to 9 PM in their time zone.)
4. Anything to always keep off LinkedIn (topics, personal posts, certain accounts)?

Then:
- Save the handle, the mode, and any keep-off rules to memory.
- If they picked auto-post, sign in to LinkedIn in your browser (use the sign-in skill; hand the screen to them for any password or 2FA step).
- Load the routines skill and create a routine on their schedule that runs the x-to-linkedin-crosspost skill.
- Do a first run right away covering the last 3 days and show them the results so they can tune the style.
